root_cause.text: The `ceph_mdsc_build_path()` function in the Ceph filesystem fails to release the memory allocated for the `path` buffer via `__putname()` when encountering error conditions (such as name encoding failures or path length limit violations) before returning, resulting in a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the addition of `__putname(path)` calls immediately before returning error pointers (`ERR_PTR(ret)`, `ERR_PTR(len)`, and `ERR_PTR(-ENAMETOOLONG)`) in `fs/ceph/mds_client.c`, which is supported by the commit message stating that these error code paths "did not free the 'path' pointer obtained by __getname()".

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
ceph: give up on paths longer than PATH_MAX

If the full path to be built by ceph_mdsc_build_path() happens to be
longer
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 550f7ca98ee028a606aa75705a7e77b1bd11720f
Author: Max Kellermann <max.kellermann@ionos.com>
Date:   Mon Nov 18 23:28:28 2024 +0100

    ceph: give up on paths longer than PATH_MAX
    
    If the full path to be built by ceph_mdsc_build_path() happens to be
    longer than PATH_MAX, then this function will enter an endless (retry)
    loop, effectively blocking the whole task.  Most of the machine
    becomes unusable, making this a very simple and effective DoS
    vulnerability.
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit replaces a retry loop with a direct return of `ERR_PTR(-ENAMETOOLONG)` when `pos < 0` (indicating the path is longer than PATH_MAX). However, it does so without releasing the allocated `path` buffer (via `__putname(path)`), which leads to a memory leak on this error path.
